title: Preparation and Imaging of Monhysterid Nematodes from the Great Salt Lake with a Scanning Electron Microscope
content: The south arm of the Great Salt Lake is four times more saline than the oceans and is a model environment for studying extremophiles. The discovery of nematodes in lake microbialites has increased the number of metazoans in the benthic zone from two to three, providing even more potential for understanding extremophile evolution [1]. Unfortunately, consumptive water use is destroying this unique habitat, so studying the lake now is important to learn how organisms have evolved to such extreme conditions [2]. To properly understand and classify these nematodes, we used an electron microscope to image important aspects of their morphology.
